ArcTrader Platform Overview

ArcTrader is DayTraders’ in-house trading platform built to give traders access to charting, order placement, account management, and market monitoring tools in one workspace.

Updated over a week ago
Copy for LLM

 

Use your Rithmic credentials to sign into ArcTrader

 

With ArcTrader, traders can view charts, monitor symbols, manage orders, track positions, use Depth of Market, access watchlists, and manage account activity directly from the platform.

 

ArcTrader includes many advanced charting features, including multiple chart layouts, chart trading tools, order tickets, bid/ask lines, Japanese chart types, drawing tools, and more.

 

What is ArcTrader?

ArcTrader allows traders to:

View live charts

Search and select symbols

Place trades

Manage open positions

Review working orders

Monitor account status

View account balance and P&L

Access order entry tools

Use Depth of Market

Organize symbols and layouts

Use drawing tools and indicators

Main Platform Areas

ArcTrader may include:

Trading

Main trading workspace

Used for charts, orders, positions, and account activity

Copier

Used for copy trading functionality when available

Stats

Used to review account or performance-related information when available

Chart Area

Displays the selected symbol and price movement

Order Ticket

Used to place Market, Limit, and Stop orders

DOM

Used to view Depth of Market and place orders from the ladder when supported

Account Manager

Displays positions, orders, order history, account balance, P&L, and drawdown information

What Can You Do in ArcTrader?

Depending on your account access, ArcTrader may allow you to:

Select a trading account

Select a market symbol

Change chart timeframe

Add indicators

Use drawing tools

Place Buy or Sell orders

Use Market, Limit, and Stop orders

Add Take Profit exits

Add Stop Loss exits

View open positions

View working orders

Review order history

View account status

View account balance

View open P&L

View daily closed P&L

View drawdown information

Flatten open positions

How to Sign into ArcTrader

ArcTrader can be accessed directly through the ArcTrader platform link using your Rithmic login credentials from your DayTraders member dashboard.

Updated over a week ago
Copy for LLM

 

 

Before You Start

Make sure you have:

An active DayTraders account

Your Rithmic username

Your Rithmic password

Access to the ArcTrader platform

Where to Find Your Rithmic Credentials

 

Your Rithmic credentials can be found in your DayTraders member dashboard.

To locate them:

Go to: https://daytraders.com/member/dashboard

Log in to your DayTraders account

Locate the account you want to trade

Copy or note your Rithmic username and password

These credentials are required to sign in to ArcTrader through the Rithmic connection.

How to Sign In to ArcTrader

To sign in:

Go to: https://arctrader.com/platform/

On the login screen, select Rithmic

Enter your Rithmic username

Enter your Rithmic password

Click Connect

Once connected, ArcTrader will load your trading workspace.

Important Notes

Please keep the following in mind:

Make sure Rithmic is selected before logging in.

Use the Rithmic credentials provided inside your member dashboard.

Enter the username and password exactly as shown.

Passwords are case-sensitive.

If your credentials were recently created, allow a few moments before trying again.

If You Cannot Log In

If you are unable to connect:

Confirm that you selected Rithmic

Recheck your Rithmic username and password

Make sure there are no extra spaces when copying your credentials

Refresh the ArcTrader page

Try logging out of the DayTraders dashboard and back in

Confirm your account is active in your dashboard

If the issue continues, contact support with:

Your account number

A screenshot of the login issue

The system selected on the ArcTrader login screen

Any error message shown

Summary

To sign in to ArcTrader:

Open https://arctrader.com/platform/

Get your Rithmic credentials from https://daytraders.com/member/dashboard

Select Rithmic

Enter your username and password

Click Connect

Getting Started: From Sign-Up to First Payout
Getting Started: From Sign-Up to First Payout

The steps from buying your first account to your first payout, and when you can start trading.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Here's the path from sign-up to your first payout on an evaluation plan (Trail, Static or EOD).

Buy an account. Register and verify your email, then choose a plan, size and billing (Monthly or Lifetime) at daytraders.com/#pricing. Accounts can't be changed after purchase.

Sign your Rithmic agreements. Use the Platform Login Details on your Dashboard to sign online or on your first rTrader Pro login: accept the first CME document and choose Non-Professional on the second.

Log in to your platform. Use the same Platform Login Details. In rTrader Pro, select DayTraders.com as the system and Chicago as the gateway. We recommend Onyx.

Trade. The trading day runs 6:00 PM–4:59 PM ET. Track your progress on your Dashboard.

Pass. Reach the profit target with the required Qualifying Days and consistency, without touching the drawdown. Then stop trading and don't cancel the evaluation. Dashboard charts and the pass email can take until midnight ET to update.

Activate your Pro Account. Within 10 days, open the Funded Accounts tab, sign the Pro Account Agreement and pay $5. It's active within 30 minutes; restart your platform to see it.

Request payouts. Set up your Payout Method (Plane or DT Wallet), meet your plan's payout rules and click Request Payout. The minimum is $500.

When can I start trading?

There's no waiting period after purchase. You'll get an email once your account is set up, and most traders are trading within 24 hours.

S2F accounts skip steps 5 and 6: you trade for payouts from day one. After passing S2L, you upload your live documents and sign the live account agreement instead.

Logging In and Credentials

Member (Dashboard) login vs Rithmic platform credentials, account numbers, and fixes for common login problems.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

You have two separate logins: one for the DayTraders website and one for your trading platform.

Login

	

Used for

	

Where to find it




Member login

	

Your Dashboard: purchases, invoices, Pro Account activation and payouts

	

The username and password you created at sign-up




Platform Login Details (User ID, e.g. DT-0009)

	

Rithmic: rTrader Pro, Onyx and other platforms, and the Rithmic agreements

	

On your Dashboard, assigned automatically

Your Account Number (e.g. DT-0009-10) is the User ID plus an account suffix. It's shown on your Dashboard and in your platform; quote it when you contact support.

 

Can't log in to your platform?

Use the Platform Login Details, not your member password. Copy and paste them: they're case-sensitive and extra spaces break them.

Sign your Rithmic agreements first, and use the latest rTrader Pro.

Select DayTraders.com as the system (not Rithmic Paper Trading) and Chicago as the gateway.

"Too many attempts - try later": after 5 failed attempts, wait about 5 minutes and try again.

Markets are closed 5:00–6:00 PM ET daily and from Friday 5:00 PM to Sunday 6:00 PM ET, so logins may fail then.

"Order Plant Guardian has disabled your User ID" usually means weekend Rithmic maintenance. Try again after 6:00 PM ET Sunday.

You can't log in without an active account, and an incorrect address or zip code in your profile can block access.

Can't log in to your Dashboard?

Check that you completed registration and confirmed your email, then use the forgot password link to reset your password. Still stuck? Contact support with your Account Number.

To see the maximum number of accounts per account type, check out the FAQ: Maximum Number of Accounts

 

Which plan is for you

Trail: Larger drawdown and no DLL, follows highest peak equity (includes open positions).

Static: You want a fixed drawdown level that never moves, for predictable risk.

EOD: You want the drawdown to move only at the end of the day, not with every intraday high.

S2F: You want to skip the evaluation and trade for payouts from day one.

S2L: You want a set path to a live account in live markets.

How to Request a Payout

Set up your Payout Method with Plane, request a payout from a Pro or S2F account, timing, and what voids a payout.

Updated over 3 weeks ago
Copy for LLM

Payouts from Pro and S2F accounts start at $500, in $50 increments. Your plan sets its own Qualifying Day, consistency and balance rules.

 

1. Set up your Payout Method (one time)

On your Dashboard, open Payout Method and fill in the required fields: US citizen or US taxpayer status, government ID or passport number, Payout Type (Plane) and Payout Email (the email you'll use for Plane). Click Update.

Plane emails you an invitation (subject similar to "Your Plane Account Setup"). Click Get Started.

Create your Plane account and sign the contract digitally.

Add your bank details in Plane.

The Payout Method fields on your Dashboard.

Important: you can't request a payout until a bank account is added in Plane.

Prefer the DT Wallet? Choose it when you request: it's credited on approval, but can't be withdrawn as cash.

 

2. Request a payout

Click Request Payout on your Dashboard and select the account.

Enter the amount in USD, agree to the terms and complete the CAPTCHA.

Submit, then place at least one trade so the payout appears on your charts.

The day a payout is approved doesn't count as a Qualifying Day. Payouts approved before the daily reports load (5:00–6:00 PM ET) are reflected the same day. You'll get an email once it's approved.

Timing matters: what counts is when your payout is approved and debited, not when you request it. If you request before 5:00 PM ET but the payout is approved and debited after 5:00 PM ET, it appears on your charts the next day, and the amount is deducted from your account balance the next day. Place a small trade on the day it's approved so the payout shows when the reports load the following day.

 

What voids a payout

Rule violations, such as hedging or high-frequency trading.

Fraud or account sharing, which also removes you from the platform.

A balance below your plan's minimum after the withdrawal.

A breach after requesting, unless the payout was already approved.

If you're called to live: moving to live is at the firm's discretion. All payout requests you submit that day are added together. At $10,000 or more, half is paid to your Payout Method and half becomes your live account's max drawdown. Under $10,000, you choose: 100% of the payout plus free S2L evaluations, or put $1,000–$10,000 toward live as your max drawdown and receive the rest. Excess simulated balances are generally forfeited, but they may be used as performance rewards in live, subject to the Risk Team's discretion. If you are not comfortable with this, do not build large excess simulated balances.

 

Payout rules by account type

Intraday Trail: Trail Payouts

Static: Static Payouts

EOD Trail: EOD Payouts

S2F (Straight-to-Sim-Funded): S2F Payouts

Live & S2L: Live Payouts

Understanding Futures Contracts And When To Roll
Understanding Futures Contracts And When To Roll

Futures contracts expire monthly. Traders can close, roll over, or settle positions to avoid delivery and maintain market exposure.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM
Lifespan of a Futures Contract

Futures contracts have a defined lifespan, and understanding this can significantly affect your trading strategy and exit decisions. Two key aspects to keep in mind are expiration and rollover.

 

Contract Expiration Explained

The expiration date of a futures contract marks the last day on which you can trade that contract. This usually happens on the third Friday of the expiration month but can vary depending on the specific contract.

 

** Important Note: Certain instruments have different rollover and expiration dates. Please ensure you verify the specific dates for the instrument you are trading. Access all relevant dates and quotes here.

 

Before the contract expires, you have three main options:

 

Close Your Position

Closing your position is the most common and straightforward way to exit a trade. By doing so, you can realize any gains or losses without having to deal with the actual physical or cash delivery of the underlying asset.

 

To close a position, you execute an opposite transaction of equal size. For instance, if you are short two WTI Crude Oil contracts that expire in September, you would need to buy two WTI Crude Oil contracts expiring in the same month. The difference between your original trade and the close will determine your profit or loss.

 

Rollover to a New Contract

Rollover refers to the process of shifting your position from an expiring contract to one with a later expiration date. Traders typically decide when to roll over by monitoring the volume of both the current and next contract months. When the new contract month’s volume reaches a certain threshold, traders may choose to switch.

 

To roll forward, you close your current position while simultaneously establishing a new one in the next contract month. For example, if you hold four S&P 500 futures contracts expiring in September, you would sell those and buy four new contracts expiring in December or a later month.

 

Settlement at Expiration

If you don’t close or roll your position before the contract’s expiration, the contract will go to settlement. This means you will be obligated to fulfill the terms of the contract. If you're holding a short position, this could involve delivering the underlying asset, either physically or through a cash settlement, depending on the type of contract.

 

Managing Expiration and Rollover

Having a strategy for handling contract expiration and rollover is essential to effective futures trading. Your approach will directly influence the outcome of your trades, making it crucial to decide in advance whether you plan to close, roll over, or settle your positions. You can learn more directly from the CME here: Understanding Futures Expiration & Contract Roll

Ensure you are trading the most current contract month with the highest volume for your instrument. Account breaches due to trading the incorrect contract will not be refunded or reset. Market Orders vs. Limit Orders
Market Orders vs. Limit Orders

Market vs limit orders in one table: speed vs price, slippage and an NQ example.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

A market order fills right away at the best available price. A limit order fills only at your chosen price or better. In short: market orders prioritize speed, limit orders prioritize price.

 

 

	

Market order

	

Limit order




Priority

	

Speed

	

Price




Fill price

	

Not guaranteed; slippage possible

	

Your price or better




Execution

	

Almost always fills quickly

	

May not fill at all




Good for

	

Quick entries and exits, emergency exits

	

Planned entries, profit targets

Example (NQ)

Bid 19,800.75 / Ask 19,801.75. A market buy usually fills near the ask (19,801.75), but can fill higher if price moves fast. A buy limit at 19,795.00 fills only at 19,795.00 or lower, and stays open if price never gets there.

 

Slippage

Slippage is the gap between the price you expected and your fill, e.g. a market buy sent at 19,801.75 that fills at 19,803.00. It's most common in fast or thin markets, around the open and close, and during news.

News trading is allowed, but liquidity can drop and volatility can rise around news, which can lead to worse fills.

Before you place an order

Check the account, symbol, Buy/Sell direction, quantity and order type, then review your open positions and working orders after submitting.

Giveaway Rules

Learn the basic eligibility rules for DayTraders giveaways, including restricted country limitations and the deadline to claim your prize.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM
Giveaway Eligibility

DayTraders giveaways are open to eligible participants only. Before entering or claiming a giveaway prize, please make sure you meet all applicable account, location, and platform requirements.

 

Important Giveaway Rules
1. Restricted Countries Are Not Eligible

Check the list of restricted countries

 

Participants located in, residing in, or registering from a restricted country are not eligible to win DayTraders giveaways.

 

If a winner is selected and we determine that they are from a restricted country, the prize cannot be awarded or redeemed.

 

DayTraders may review the winner’s account information, registration details, and eligibility before issuing any giveaway prize.

 

2. Prizes Must Be Claimed Within 7 Days

If you are selected as a giveaway winner, you must claim or redeem your prize within 7 days from the date we notify you.

 

To claim your prize, follow the instructions provided in the giveaway notification. This may include replying to an email, confirming your account details, or accepting the applicable terms.

 

If the prize is not claimed within 7 days, the offer will expire and the prize may no longer be available.

 

What Happens If I Do Not Claim My Prize in Time?

If you do not respond or complete the required redemption steps within 7 days of being notified, the giveaway prize will be forfeited.

 

Once the claim period expires, DayTraders is not required to reissue the prize or extend the deadline.

 

Can I Transfer My Giveaway Prize to Someone Else?

Giveaway prizes are intended for the selected winner only and may not be transferred, sold, or assigned to another person unless DayTraders gives written approval.

 

Final Review Before Prize Issuance

All giveaway prizes are subject to final eligibility review. DayTraders reserves the right to deny, cancel, or withhold a giveaway prize if the winner does not meet the giveaway rules or account eligibility requirements.

 

Disclaimer: Giveaway prizes have no cash value and cannot be exchanged for cash. Additional terms may apply depending on the specific giveaway.

Who Can Sign Up
Who Can Sign Up

Age requirement, signing up as an individual vs. business and non-professional status.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

To sign up with DayTraders, you need to meet a few requirements.

 

Age

You must be 18 or older to buy an evaluation or hold a Pro Account.

 

Individuals, not businesses

Register under your own legal first and last name, not an LLC, corporation or business name.

Your accounts and Pro Account Agreement stay tied to you as an individual. U.S. traders provide a Social Security number; others provide a passport or other government ID number.

To be paid as a business, set up your payout profile as a business in Plane (business name, address, EIN, bank account). No EIN is needed to sign up.

Don't create a second DayTraders account for your business. Only one DayTraders login is allowed per household.

Non-professional status

Our simulated programs, including S2L, are for non-professional traders only: people who hold Series licenses or are registered with the SEC, NFA or another regulator can't take part.

 

Restricted countries

DayTraders is available in over 100 countries, but some countries aren't eligible for new services or additional accounts because of:

Sanctions or embargoes.

Platform or broker restrictions that prevent live trading services.

Fraud risk, such as credit card fraud or identity theft.

Language or support challenges that affect our ability to offer top-tier service.

If you are a citizen of an OFAC (Office of Foreign Assets Control) or restricted country, we can't provide services to you, wherever you are located.

All transactions attempted while in a restricted country will be blocked. Attempts to circumvent this may result in account closure and suspension of our services. Contact support if you have any questions.

DT Wallet FAQ
DT Wallet FAQ

The DT Wallet allows you to receive an approved simulated payout as DayTraders account credit instead of sending the funds to your bank, if you are eligible.

Updated over a week ago
Copy for LLM

 

Wallet funds are available immediately after payout approval and can be used toward eligible purchases on DayTraders.

What is the DT Wallet?

The DT Wallet is a DayTraders account credit balance.

 

If you are eligible, you can choose to have an approved simulated payout credited to your DT Wallet instead of receiving it as a bank payout.

 

Wallet funds can be used to purchase eligible accounts on DayTraders.

How does the DT Wallet work?

When requesting a payout, you may be able to choose where the payout should go:

Bank

DT Wallet

Bank is selected by default.

 

If you select DT Wallet and your payout is approved, the funds are credited to your wallet immediately.

What is the benefit of using the DT Wallet?

The DT Wallet allows you to use approved payout funds faster.

 

Benefits include:

Instant wallet credit after payout approval

No bank transfer waiting period

No transfer fee

Ability to purchase a new eligible account right away

The trade-off is that wallet funds remain as DayTraders credit and cannot be withdrawn as cash.

Can I withdraw DT Wallet funds as cash?

No.

DT Wallet funds cannot be withdrawn as cash.

Wallet funds can only be used for eligible purchases on DayTraders.

Is the DT Wallet available for all payouts?

No.

The DT Wallet is only available for simulated account payouts if you are eligible.

Live account payouts cannot be sent to the DT Wallet and must be sent to the bank.

What is the minimum payout amount for the DT Wallet?

The minimum amount that can be sent to the DT Wallet is:

$500

If the payout amount is under $500, the wallet option will not be available.

Why do I not see the DT Wallet option on my payout request?

The DT Wallet option may not appear if:

The payout is under $500

The payout is from a live account

The payout is not eligible for wallet credit

If the wallet option is not shown, the payout will need to be requested through the available payout method.

When are DT Wallet funds available?

DT Wallet funds are available immediately after the payout is approved.

Once approved:

The payout leaves your trading account

Your wallet balance is credited

The funds can be used for eligible purchases

A confirmation email is sent with the credited amount and updated wallet balance

Can I change my payout from Wallet back to Bank?

Once the payout has been approved, the wallet selection cannot be reversed.

Wallet funds cannot be converted back into a bank payout.

Please make sure you want the payout credited to your DT Wallet before confirming your request.

Where can I view my DT Wallet balance?

You can view your wallet balance from the Wallet section in your DayTraders member area.

The Wallet page may show:

Current wallet balance

Total amount added

Total amount spent

Wallet activity history

Running balance after each wallet movement

Related account or purchase information

How can I use my DT Wallet funds?

DT Wallet funds can be used at checkout for eligible DayTraders purchases. Specifically, the DT Wallet can be used for one-time purchases of evaluations and S2L accounts, including bulk orders.

If you have an available wallet balance, the wallet payment option may appear alongside other payment options at checkout.

Can I pay part with Wallet and part with card?

No, split payments are not supported.

 

The DT Wallet must cover the full order amount. If your wallet balance does not cover the full order, you will need to use another payment method.

What happens if my wallet balance is not enough for the full order?

If your wallet balance does not cover the full order, the wallet option will not be selectable at checkout.

 

The checkout page may show:

Your available wallet balance

The remaining amount needed

A note that the wallet must cover the full order

Example:

“$500.00 available, $90.00 short. Wallet must cover the full order.”

Can I use DT Wallet funds on monthly plans, add-ons or Pro-Accounts?

No, the DT Wallet can only be used for eligible one-time purchases (Evaluations and S2L).

 

Wallet funds cannot be used on monthly plans.

Are wallet purchases refundable?

No, purchases made with DT Wallet funds are final and non-refundable.

Can I buy multiple accounts with my DT Wallet?

Yes, you can use your DT Wallet for eligible bulk purchases as long as your wallet balance covers the full order amount.

 

If the wallet balance does not cover the full order, the wallet cannot be used.

What if I use my wallet and the account does not appear?

If a purchase does not complete properly after wallet funds are used, the system may return the funds automatically and provide a reference number.

 

If you do not see the account or the returned wallet funds, contact support with:

Your account email

The purchase details

A screenshot of the issue

Any reference number shown

Important DT Wallet Rules

Please keep the following in mind:

Minimum wallet transfer: $500

Available for simulated payouts only, if you are eligible

Live payouts are not eligible

Cash withdrawals are not available

Split payments are not supported

Wallet must cover the full order  (Eligible for one-time purchases of Evaluations and S2L. Including bulk orders)

Monthly plans are not eligible

Wallet purchases are final and non-refundable

Approved wallet payouts cannot be reversed back to bank payout

Summary

The DT Wallet gives you a faster way to use approved simulated payout funds toward new DayTraders purchases, if you are eligible.

Key points:

Wallet funds are credited immediately after payout approval

Wallet funds can only be used on DayTraders

Wallet funds cannot be withdrawn as cash

Wallet funds must cover the full order (Wallet funds can be used for one-time purchases of Evaluations and S2L)

Wallet funds cannot be used on monthly plans

Wallet purchases are final

Key DayTraders terms in plain English: account types, drawdown, DLL, QDays, consistency, statuses and more.

Copy for LLM

Key DayTraders terms, using the names you'll see across the Help Center.

Term

	

Meaning




Evaluation

	

A simulated account where you prove your strategy by reaching the profit target within the rules.




Pro Account

	

The simulated funded account you activate after passing an evaluation. It earns payouts.




S2F

	

Straight to Funded: a simulated funded account with no evaluation (Instant at checkout).




S2L

	

Straight to Live: a simulated evaluation with a set path to a live account (Live at checkout).




Live account

	

An account that trades in live markets, from S2L or by invitation from the firm.




Profit target

	

The profit you need to pass an evaluation, net of commissions.




Max drawdown / drawdown level

	

The most your account can lose. The drawdown level is the balance you must stay above; touching it fails the account.




Intraday trailing / EOD trailing / Static

	

How the drawdown level moves: with your peak balance in real time, only at the end of each trading day, or never.




Daily Loss Limit (DLL)

	

The most you can lose in one trading day, measured from that day's starting balance. Hitting it pauses the account.




Trading day

	

6:00 PM to 4:59 PM ET the next day.




Minimum daily profit

	

The smallest daily profit that counts toward Qualifying Days and the activity requirement.




Qualifying Day (QDay)

	

A trading day that meets the minimum daily profit, follows the rules and ends within consistency.




Consistency

	

Your best day's profit as a percentage of your total profit. Each plan sets a maximum.




Failed / Paused / Inactive

	

Failed: the drawdown was touched and the account is closed. Paused: the DLL was hit; trading resumes at 6:00 PM ET. Inactive: the activity requirement was missed and the account is closed.




Dashboard

	

Your member area on daytraders.com for accounts, billing, activation and payouts.




Payout Method

	

Where payouts go: your bank through Plane, or your DT Wallet.




DT Wallet

	

DayTraders credit from a payout, usable for one-time purchases. It can't be withdrawn as cash.




Rithmic / rTrader Pro

	

Rithmic provides your accounts' market data and order routing; rTrader Pro is its trading platform.




Mini / micro

	

Contract sizes. 10 micros count as 1 mini toward your max contracts.




Slippage

	

The difference between the price you expected and the price your order filled at.

About DayTraders

Who DayTraders is, what is simulated, how payouts are paid, and the account types in one line each.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

DayTraders.com is an educational, non-professional trader evaluation company focused on education, risk management and trader development. You trade futures under clear rules, prove your strategy and earn payouts.

 

What's simulated

Evaluations, Pro Accounts, S2F accounts and S2L evaluations are all simulated: no real money is deposited with us or traded in the market. Only live accounts trade in live markets.

 

Payouts are real

Payouts from Pro Accounts and S2F accounts are real money, sent to your Payout Method: your bank through Plane, or as credit in your DT Wallet to spend on new accounts. Live account payouts are paid through Plane.

 

Account types

Evaluation (Trail, Static or EOD): a simulated account. Reach the profit target within the rules to pass.

Pro Account: the simulated funded account you activate for $5 after passing. It earns payouts.

S2F (Straight to Funded, shown as Instant at checkout): a simulated funded account with no evaluation.

S2L (Straight to Live, shown as Live at checkout): a simulated evaluation with a set path to a live account.

Live account: trades in live markets. You get one by passing S2L or by invitation from the firm.

Moving from a Pro Account or S2F to live is at the firm's discretion. There's no fixed milestone, and about 1% of simulated funded traders are currently moved to live. Services are for non-professional traders only.

Evaluation: the trailing drawdown stops trailing once it reaches your profit-target balance.

Pro Account: it starts again at the full max drawdown and stops at your starting balance.

How the EOD trailing drawdown works and where it stops, by size.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

EOD accounts use an end-of-day trailing drawdown: the level only moves after each trading day closes, based on your closing balance. Your balance must stay above it at all times, including intraday.

 

How it works

It starts at your starting balance minus the max drawdown.

After a day closes at a new high, it moves up to that balance minus the max drawdown. It never moves down.

It stops at your starting balance, in the evaluation and in the Pro Account.

S2F Consistency

S2F 20% consistency rule per payout cycle, with an example.

Updated over 3 weeks ago
Copy for LLM

S2F accounts use a 20% consistency rule per payout cycle: your best day can't be more than 20% of the profit made since your last payout.

 

How it's calculated

Largest single-day profit ÷ profit this cycle = consistency %

Example: $5,000 made this cycle, best day $1,200. 1,200 ÷ 5,000 = 24%, over 20%. Once cycle profit reaches $6,000, you're back within the rule.

If you're over the limit

Consistency is checked at the end of every trading day and resets after each payout. A day that ends over 20% isn't a Qualifying Day, and you can't request a payout until you're back within the rule. Keep trading to bring it down, and check your numbers with the Consistency Calculator.

S2F Drawdown

How the S2F end-of-day trailing drawdown works and where it stops, by size.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

S2F accounts use an end-of-day trailing drawdown: the level only moves after each trading day closes, based on your closing balance. Your balance must stay above it at all times, including intraday.

 

How it works

It starts at your starting balance minus the max drawdown.

After a day closes at a new high, it moves up to that balance minus the max drawdown. It never moves down.

It stops at your starting balance.

Moving from Pro or S2F to Live

How Pro and S2F traders may be invited to live and how payouts are handled when they are.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Traders with Pro Accounts or S2F accounts may be invited to a live account at the firm's discretion. There's no fixed milestone: performance, consistency and rule-following are reviewed continuously, and about 1% of simulated funded traders are currently moved to live.

 

Your live account

A Risk Manager sets your live account's parameters with you, including the starting balance. Invited accounts most likely use an EOD or static drawdown. If you're in a restricted country, the Risk Manager will discuss your options. 

 

Payouts when you're called to live

If you're called to live when you request a payout, all payout requests you submit that day are added together. For example, five $2,000 requests count as $10,000.

$10,000 or more: half is paid to your Payout Method and half becomes your live account's max drawdown.

Less than $10,000: take 100% of the payout plus free S2L evaluations (usually matched 1:1 in size, up to 5 Core or 3 Edge/Ultra), or put $1,000–$10,000 toward live as your max drawdown and receive the rest.

Scaling is discussed with the Risk Team.

 

Your other accounts

Once you're live, your simulated accounts are closed. Excess simulated balances are generally forfeited, but they may be used as performance rewards in live, subject to the Risk Team's discretion. If you are not comfortable with this, do not build large excess simulated balances.

 

Any Pro accounts that have not received a payout and are in good standing will be refunded along with their respective evaluations.

How to pass

Reach the profit target.

Trade at least 8 Qualifying Days: days that meet the minimum daily profit, follow the rules and end within consistency.

Keep your best day at or below 25% of your total profit.

After you pass

Stop trading; the evaluation closes once it passes. Reach out to support and ask for the risk team to review your accounts. 

 

Then, once the Live Docs page is enabled on your dashboard (if it isn't already), upload your live documents and sign the live account agreement on your Dashboard. 

 

Your live account is set up within 1–5 business days.

Important: once you're live, all your simulated accounts (including other S2L evaluations) are closed, and you can't buy new S2L evaluations while you're trading live.

Good to know

No time limit and no resets.

You can have as many S2L evaluations as you like, however you can only have up to 5 live accounts.

S2L Consistency
S2L Consistency

S2L 25% consistency rule with an example. Live accounts have no consistency rule.

October 23, 2026
Copy for LLM

S2L evaluations use a 25% consistency rule: your best day can't be more than 25% of your total profit. Live accounts have no consistency rule.

 

How it's calculated

Largest single-day profit ÷ total profit = consistency %

Example (Core): total profit $3,200, best day $900. 900 ÷ 3,200 = 28%, over 25%. Once total profit reaches $3,600, you're back within the rule.

If you're over the limit

Consistency is checked at the end of every trading day. A day that ends over 25% isn't a Qualifying Day, and you can't pass until you're back within the rule. Keep trading to bring it down, and check your numbers with the Consistency Calculator.

Live Payouts

Live payouts: 80/20 split, $1,000 buffer, when payouts unlock and how they're processed.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Live accounts pay an 80/20 profit split, with no minimum daily profit or consistency rule. Requests start at $500, in $50 increments.

 

When you can request

Payouts unlock once your drawdown has locked at your starting balance. You can withdraw any profit above a $1,000 buffer without limit. You can trade into the buffer, but not withdraw it. This is to guarantee at least $1000 of trading room after a payout.

 

Plan

Edge

Ultra

How it's processed

You request a payout from your Dashboard.

The firm locks the account.

The payout is debited and approved, and sent through Plane.

The account is ready to trade again.

Requests are processed between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM ET on business days; later requests are processed the next business day. If your balance drops below starting balance + $1,000 before processing, the payout is skipped and you can request again once you're back above it.

 

Firm-invited live accounts

These most likely use an EOD or static drawdown and follow the same steps. If your EOD drawdown hasn't locked yet, step 3 happens after it updates in Rithmic between 5:00 and 6:00 PM ET.

Copy for LLM

A live account trades in live markets. You get one by passing an S2L evaluation, or by invitation from the firm. This article covers live accounts from S2L.

More than one live account

You can have up to 5 live accounts from S2L at a time. All of them appear in your trading platform, but only one is tradeable at a time:

Your first live account is tradeable.

Once its drawdown locks at your starting balance, or the account is breached, a Risk Manager makes the next account tradeable during business hours.

This repeats for each of your live accounts.

The reason for this is to give traders the best chance at staying in the live environment longer as well as preventing 1-2 day wash outs.

 

If you've passed more than 5 S2L evaluations, you'll see the first 5. The others are loaded as earlier accounts are closed and removed from your Dashboard.

 

Platforms

Onyx is offered on live accounts and the free version of Quantower is available. Other platforms need a paid license; NinjaTrader isn't supported, but some have reported success connecting.

 

Good to know

Once you're live, all your simulated accounts are closed and you can't buy new S2L evaluations while trading live. You cannot trade in sim and live at the same time.

If the account touches the drawdown level, it's closed. You can qualify again with a new S2L evaluation; there's no cooldown.

Minimum Activity Policy
Minimum Activity Policy

How many trading days you need to keep an account active, how the rolling 30-day window works and what happens if you miss it.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

To keep an account active, you need a minimum number of trading days that meet the minimum daily profit for your account size in every rolling 30-day window.

 

What you need

Billing

	

Requirement




Monthly

	

At least 1 trading day meeting the minimum daily profit in every rolling 30-day window




Lifetime (one-time, including bulk purchases)

	

At least 4 trading days meeting the minimum daily profit in every rolling 30-day window

The window starts on the purchase date for every account, including accounts bought in bulk.

Days don't need to be consecutive.

Consistency isn't required. A day counts if it meets the minimum daily profit, even if it isn't a Qualifying Day.

The check runs every day on the most recent 30 days, so keep trading regularly rather than completing the days once.

Example

Lifetime account bought January 1: you meet the minimum daily profit on January 3, 8, 15 and 22. At the first review on January 30, the account is active. On February 3, the window is January 4 to February 3 and January 3 drops out. Unless you've had another qualifying trading day by then, only 3 remain and the account becomes Inactive.

If you miss the requirement

The account is marked Inactive and closed. Inactive accounts can't be reactivated, and a Monthly account stops rebilling. You'll need to buy a new account to continue.

 

You can track your trading days on your Dashboard.

No Martingale
No Martingale

Why doubling your position size after losing trades (Martingale) is prohibited on every plan, and how it differs from DCA.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

The Martingale strategy, or doubling down after losses, is prohibited on every plan and every instrument.

 

What counts as Martingale

Martingale means increasing your size on each new trade after a losing trade to win back the loss. Increasing your position size by 2x or more after a closed loss, as part of this pattern, isn't allowed.

Example: you trade 2 NQ and close at a loss. Your next trade is 4 NQ, another loss, then 8 NQ, and so on until you win or the account fails. This is Martingale.

What's allowed

Adding to an open position within your max contracts is Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA), which is allowed. Martingale is about the size of new trades after closed losses.

 

Consequences

Trading activity is monitored for doubling-down patterns. If a prohibited strategy is confirmed, all accounts involved are closed and unpaid profits on them are forfeited. Serious or repeat violations lead to a full ban. Payouts approved before the finding are honored.

No High-Frequency Trading
No High-Frequency Trading

High-frequency trading (HFT) is prohibited on every plan. Here's what counts as HFT and what happens if it's detected.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

High-Frequency Trading (HFT) isn't allowed on any account. Automation is allowed as long as it doesn't trade in an HFT style.

 

What counts as HFT

Systems that place, modify or cancel orders in milliseconds or at extremely high speed.

Executing hundreds or thousands of trades per second or minute.

Order spamming, or repeatedly placing and canceling orders at high speed.

Latency-based strategies that exploit price differences in milliseconds or microseconds.

Excessive trade volume over very short periods.

Why it's prohibited

HFT creates unfair advantages and can overload trading systems. Keeping it out gives every trader the same conditions.

 

Consequences

Trade frequency, volume and execution patterns are monitored. An account suspected of HFT is suspended pending review. If a prohibited strategy is confirmed, all accounts involved are closed and unpaid profits on them are forfeited. Serious or repeat violations lead to a full ban. Payouts approved before the finding are honored.

Hedging (holding opposite positions in the same or related instruments) is prohibited within and across your accounts.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Hedging is prohibited within an account and across your accounts.

 

What counts as hedging

Holding long and short positions in the same instrument at the same time, in one account or across your DayTraders accounts. For example, long NQ in one account and short NQ in another.

Opposite positions in related or correlated instruments, such as long NQ in one account and short ES in another.

Opposite positions coordinated with other people.

What's allowed

Trading with other firms is allowed, and so is copying the same trades across your own accounts.

 

Consequences

Trade execution across accounts and related instruments is monitored. If a prohibited strategy is confirmed, all accounts involved are closed and unpaid profits on them are forfeited. Serious or repeat violations lead to a full ban. Payouts approved before the finding are honored.

Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA)
Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA)

DCA (adding to an open position) is allowed on every plan within your max contracts. Here's how it differs from Martingale.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA) is allowed on every plan: evaluations, Pro Accounts, S2F, S2L and live accounts.

 

What DCA is

DCA means building a position in parts at different prices instead of entering all at once, so your average entry price reflects each fill. It's allowed as long as your total open position stays within your max contracts.

Example (10-contract account): you buy 2 ES, then add 2 more at a lower price. Your 4 contracts have one average entry price, and you're still within your 10-contract limit.

Your drawdown level and any Daily Loss Limit still apply to the whole position, including open losses.

 

DCA vs Martingale

 

	

DCA (allowed)

	

Martingale (prohibited)




What you do

	

Add to an open position

	

Double the size of new trades after closed losses




Size limit

	

Within your max contracts

	

Keeps growing until a win or the account fails

Repeatedly doubling size on new trades after losses is Martingale, even if each trade stays within your max contracts.

Trading Hours, Holidays and Overnight Positions
Trading Hours, Holidays and Overnight Positions

When the trading day starts and ends, how holidays are handled, and the rules for overnight positions, auto-liquidation and news.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

The trading day runs from 6:00 PM ET to 4:59 PM ET the next day. Sunday's 6:00 PM ET session counts as part of Monday.

 

Market close and holidays

Close trades by 4:59 PM ET. Some markets, such as agricultural futures, close earlier.

On a market holiday, the session isn't a trading day and its trades count toward the next trading day.

Shortened sessions that aren't holidays, such as Black Friday and Christmas Eve, count as normal trading days.

Check the CME Group Holiday Calendar for early closes.

Overnight and weekend positions

Holding positions overnight or over the weekend is allowed but not recommended, because of mark-to-market adjustments. DayTraders doesn't close your positions for you at the end of the session.

 

Auto-liquidation

There's no firm-set liquidation time. Rithmic auto-liquidates only when you hit your drawdown level or Daily Loss Limit, and the account shows "Admin Only" until it resets. You can set your own time in rTrader Pro: right-click the account, choose View risk parameters and set the auto-liquidation time. It doesn't adjust for daylight saving time.

 

News trading

Trading around news is allowed but not recommended. Fast markets can hit daily price limits or cause platform lag, and losses from these conditions aren't covered.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Your max contracts is the largest total open position you can hold at once, across all instruments combined.

 

How it's counted

10 micro contracts count as 1 mini contract.

Positions in different instruments add up. On a 10-contract account, 5 NQ + 50 MNQ uses your full limit.

Working orders don't count until they fill.

An order that would take you over the limit is rejected.

Rule Violations and Account Status

What Failed, Paused and Inactive mean, why you see 'Only Admins Can Place Trades', penalties for violations and what to do after failing.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Your account status shows whether you can keep trading. Here's what each one means.

Account statuses

Status

	

What happened

	

What it means




Failed

	

Your balance touched the drawdown level.

	

The account is closed and can't be reset.




Paused

	

You hit the Daily Loss Limit.

	

Open positions are closed and trading resumes at 6:00 PM ET, when the next trading day starts. The account isn't failed.




Inactive

	

You missed the Minimum Activity Policy.

	

The account is closed and can't be reactivated.

"Only Admins Can Place Trades"

This message in your platform means trading is disabled: the account has hit its drawdown level (failed) or its Daily Loss Limit (paused until the next trading day).

Rule violations

If a prohibited strategy is confirmed, all accounts involved are closed and unpaid profits on them are forfeited. Serious or repeat violations lead to a full ban. Payouts approved before the finding are honored.

After failing

Buy a new evaluation from your Dashboard. Resets aren't available, and you can start again as many times as you like.

A failed Monthly account stops rebilling, including a failed Pro Account.

To skip the evaluation, you can buy an S2F account instead.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

A Qualifying Day (QDay) is a trading day that counts toward passing an evaluation or toward a payout.

 

What counts as a QDay

You meet or exceed the minimum daily profit for your account size.

You follow all trading rules.

The day ends within your plan's consistency limit.

The day is a trading day (6:00 PM ET to 4:59 PM ET the next day).

The day you request a payout doesn't count as a QDay.

 

It is possible for a day to have recorded profit greater than the minimum required amount but not be counted as a Qday. This is because the day has either broken a rule or is above the consistency percentage. 

 

These percentages are re-calculated every day after reports load, so as profit is generated the % of total profit that day counts as is reduced. Once it is calculated to be within the consistency limit, it will be counted as a Qday.

Live accounts have no QDay or minimum daily profit requirement.

 

QDays vs TDays

TDays (Trading Days) count every day you traded, whether or not it qualified. Both appear on your Dashboard. The Minimum Activity Policy counts days that meet the minimum daily profit, even if they aren't QDays.

Affiliate commission reports are generated on the first day of each month. Compensation for the previous period is processed and sent by the 15th.

For example, commissions earned between August 1 and August 31 will be reported on September 1, with payment processed by September 15.

 

Your payment should arrive in your bank account within 3-7 business days after the 15th, depending on your bank’s processing speed.

 

Please wait a full 7 business days before submitting a support ticket regarding your payment. Sometimes banks can be slow, so patience is appreciated.

 

The minimum compensation threshold is $100 with any given month. If you don’t reach $100 in a month, your earnings will roll over to the next month until you do. For example, if you earn $30 in June, no compensation will be processed in July. But if you earn $100 in July, bringing your total to $130, you’ll receive payment on August 15.

 

Affiliate Requirements for Commission: To qualify for a commission, affiliates must meet the following criteria within the calendar month:

3 new paying customers

50 clicks

$100 in commissions

Market, Limit, and Stop Orders

ArcTrader allows traders to choose between different order types depending on how they want to enter or manage a trade.

Updated over a week ago
Copy for LLM

 

The most common order types are:

Market

Limit

Stop

Market Orders

 

A Market order is used to buy or sell immediately at the best available market price.

Market orders are commonly used when:

You want immediate execution

Speed is more important than exact price

The market is liquid

You are entering quickly

You are exiting quickly

Important notes:

Market orders do not guarantee a specific fill price.

The final fill price may differ from the displayed price.

Slippage can occur during fast market movement.

Market orders should be used carefully during volatile periods.

Limit Orders

 

A Limit order is used to buy or sell at a specific price or better.

Limit orders are commonly used when:

You want a specific entry price

You do not want to chase the market

You are waiting for price to pull back

You want more control over execution price

Important notes:

Limit orders do not guarantee execution.

Price must reach your limit level.

The order may remain working if the market does not trade at that level.

The market can move away without filling your order.

Stop Orders

 

A Stop order becomes active once price reaches the stop level.

Stop orders are commonly used when:

Entering after a breakout

Exiting a losing trade

Protecting a position

Managing risk

Important notes:

Stop orders may trigger during fast market movement.

Once triggered, execution may occur at a different price.

Stop orders do not always guarantee the exact stop price.

Slippage may occur.

Best Practices

When choosing an order type:

Use Market orders carefully during volatility.

Use Limit orders when price control matters.

Use Stop orders when managing risk or breakout entries.

Always confirm order direction.

Review order levels before submitting.

Confirm whether the order is Buy or Sell.

Summary

Market, Limit, and Stop orders give traders different ways to enter and manage trades.

Choosing the correct order type is important for:

Execution

Risk management

Trade planning

What is Take Profit?

 

 

Take Profit is an exit order designed to close a trade at a selected profit target.

Traders may use Take Profit to:

Lock in gains

Set a planned exit level

Reduce emotional decision-making

Automate part of trade management

Close a trade when price reaches a target

What is Stop Loss?

 

 

Stop Loss is an exit order designed to close a trade if price moves against the position.

Traders may use Stop Loss to:

Limit downside risk

Follow a trading plan

Avoid holding losing trades too long

Protect account drawdown

Manage risk more consistently

How Can Exits Be Set?

Depending on platform availability, exits may be configured by:

Price

Ticks

Risk amount

Other supported settings

Important Notes

Please keep the following in mind:

Take Profit and Stop Loss settings should be reviewed before submitting.

Exit orders may be affected by fast market conditions.

Stop Loss orders do not guarantee an exact fill price.

Exit levels may need to meet platform or symbol requirements.

Traders are responsible for confirming their risk before placing trades.

Best Practices

Before using exits:

Confirm your entry order first.

Choose a realistic profit target.

Use a stop level that matches your risk plan.

Avoid placing stops too close to normal market noise.

Confirm whether exits are attached correctly.

Review active orders after placing the trade.

Understanding Account Colors in rTrader Pro

Learn what the colors in rTrader Pro mean for your account and why they are irrelevant for DayTraders.com prop trading accounts.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM
1. Why does my account display different colors in rTrader Pro?

In rTrader Pro, you may notice that your account is displayed in various colors such as green, gray, red, or yellow. These colors are part of rTrader Pro's default settings and can be found under the "Legend" section of the platform. However, they are not relevant to your account's actual status when trading with DayTraders.com.
​

 

2. Should I be concerned about the account colors?

No, the colors you see in rTrader Pro are not important and do not reflect the true status of your account. The color system was not designed for prop trading firms like DayTraders.com, so it does not accurately represent your account's performance or status.

 

3. What does DayTraders.com monitor for account status?

At DayTraders.com, we only focus on the actual numbers in your account, such as your balance and active status. As long as your account is marked "active" and your balance is above the projected auto-liquidation threshold, your account is considered to be in good standing.

 

4. Where can I find more information about my account metrics?

To better understand what each column and number means in rTrader Pro, you can learn more by clicking > HERE <.

 

If you have any further questions, feel free to reach out to our support team.

Onyx Platform FAQ (Rithmic-Powered)

Learn how Onyx works with Rithmic, including market hours, maintenance windows, login access, and account processing.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM
What is the Onyx platform?

Onyx is our trading platform hosted and powered by Rithmic. It uses Rithmic’s professional futures trading infrastructure for order routing, execution, and market data, while using full TradingView charts.

 

If you are familiar with Rithmic-based platforms, Onyx operates on the same backend technology.

Is Onyx powered by Rithmic?

Yes. Onyx is fully powered by Rithmic.

This means:

Orders are routed through Rithmic

Market data is provided by Rithmic

Platform availability follows Rithmic market hours and maintenance schedules

Where can I view my trade history?

All Onyx trade history can be accessed through rTrader Pro.

You can view:

Executed trades

Order fills and timestamps

Account-level trade history

Even if you trade using a different front-end, rTrader Pro is the source of record for all Onyx accounts.

When are Onyx accounts created and processed?

Account purchases made during market close are not processed immediately.

This includes purchases made:

On weekends

During daily market maintenance

Accounts will be processed closer to market open, once Rithmic systems are fully online.

This delay is normal and expected.

What are the futures market hours (ET)?

Onyx follows the standard CME futures schedule:

Market Open (ET):

Sunday at 6:00 PM ET

Market Close (ET):

Friday at 5:00 PM ET

Daily Maintenance Window (ET):

Monday–Friday from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM ET

Can I log in during market close or maintenance?

In most cases, no.

During:

Weekends

The daily 5:00–6:00 PM ET maintenance window

Rithmic performs system maintenance. During this time, you may be unable to:

Log in to the platform

Sign agreements

Complete account creation

Access account credentials

This is expected Rithmic behavior and does not indicate an issue with your account.

I can’t log in — is something wrong with my account?

Most likely no.

If you are attempting to log in during:

A weekend

The daily Rithmic maintenance window

Please wait until the market reopens. Access will restore automatically once maintenance is complete.
​

Submitting a support ticket during these times will not speed up access.
​

Lag & Order Synchronization

Experiencing a delay on your chart or difficulty adjusting orders is typically tied to internet upload speed or high latency (ping). When your connection is unstable, your browser struggles to send command signals to the Rithmic servers.
​

Common Symptoms:

Inability to move Take Profit (TP) or Stop Loss (SL) bracket orders.

Orders appearing "stuck" or not moving on the chart.

Inability to close an active position.

Chart price action appearing frozen or delayed.

How to Resolve Lag Issues

If you encounter these issues, take the following steps immediately to secure your positions:

Immediate Refresh: Press F5 on your keyboard to resync the data feed and refresh the connection.

Use a Wired Connection: Switch from Wi-Fi to an Ethernet cable. This provides a stable data flow and significantly reduces latency spikes.

 

Try Incognito Mode: Open the platform in a private/incognito window. This ensures browser extensions aren't interfering with or slowing down your data feed.

Manual Trade Management: If a refresh doesn't resolve the visual lag, we recommend closing the trade manually via the positions tab to avoid unintended losses due to price discrepancies.

Onyx DOM (Depth of Market)
Onyx DOM (Depth of Market)
October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

The DOM (Depth of Market) in Onyx provides a real-time view of bid and ask liquidity at each price level, allowing traders to see market depth and execute trades directly from the ladder.

 

The DOM is designed for speed, precision, and active order flow trading.

 

What the DOM Shows

The Onyx DOM displays:

Bid column (green): Buy orders waiting below the market

Ask column (red): Sell orders waiting above the market

Price ladder: Each row represents a valid tick price

Current price: Highlighted in the center of the ladder

Order size: Number of contracts resting at each price level

This gives you a clear picture of supply and demand in real time.

DOM Controls Explained

Across the top of the DOM you’ll see:

SELL: Click to submit sell orders at the selected price

BID: Shows buy-side liquidity

RECENTER: Re-centers the ladder around current price

ASK: Shows sell-side liquidity

BUY: Click to submit buy orders at the selected price

You can interact directly with the ladder to place orders quickly.

Trading from the DOM

You can place orders directly by clicking on the ladder:

Click on the Bid side to place a buy order

Click on the Ask side to place a sell order

Orders respect your current Order Entry settings

Bracket logic and quantity apply if enabled

This makes the DOM ideal for scalping and fast execution strategies.

Top of Book

The Top of Book view focuses on the best bid and best ask prices only.

 

This is useful when:

You want a simplified view

You are trading very fast markets

You don’t need full depth

Common Use Cases

The Onyx DOM is commonly used for:

Scalping and short-term trades

Order flow analysis

Liquidity-based entries

Fast manual execution

Monitoring absorption and stacking

Best Practices

Use the DOM with a wired internet connection

Combine DOM trading with bracket orders for risk control

Recenter frequently in fast markets

Avoid DOM trading on unstable connections

Practice in simulation before live trading

Important Notes

DOM data is powered by Rithmic

Execution speed depends on your gateway selection and network quality

Liquidity can change instantly during volatile conditions

Summary

The Onyx DOM gives traders direct access to market depth and rapid execution through an intuitive ladder interface. It is a powerful tool for active futures traders who rely on precision, speed, and real-time liquidity visibility.

Order Entry in Onyx
Order Entry in Onyx
October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

The Order Entry panel in Onyx gives you complete control over how trades are placed and managed. Whether you are submitting a quick market order or creating a full risk-managed trade, Onyx provides precise control with professional-grade tools.

 


​

Understanding Order Types

 

 

Market Order

Definition: An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available current price.

Best For: When speed is your priority and you want to enter or exit a position "right now."

Note: In fast-moving markets, the price you receive may differ slightly from the price you saw when clicking the button (known as slippage).

Limit Order

Definition: An order to buy or sell only at a specific price or better.

A Buy Limit is placed below the current market price.

A Sell Limit is placed above the current market price.

Best For: When you want to control your entry price and are willing to wait for the market to come to you.

Note: Your order will only be filled if the market reaches your price. There is no guarantee of execution.

Stop Order (Stop-Market)

Definition: An order that remains "hidden" until the market hits a specific trigger price (the "Stop Price"). Once triggered, it instantly becomes a Market Order.

Best For: Protecting against losses (Stop-Loss) or entering a trade when the price breaks through a key level.

Note: Because it becomes a Market Order upon triggering, it guarantees execution but does not guarantee a specific price.

Stop Limit Order

Definition: A combination of a Stop Order and a Limit Order. Once the market hits your Stop Price, it triggers a Limit Order instead of a Market Order.

Best For: Traders who want to enter on a breakout but are unwilling to pay more than a certain amount if the market gaps or moves too quickly.

Note: This provides the most control over price, but carries the risk that your order may not be filled if the price moves past your Limit Price too fast.

Bracket Configuration

Bracket orders automate your risk management by placing exit orders the moment you enter a trade. This ensures you have a plan to lock in gains and protect your capital.

Take Profit (TP): Closes your position at a target price to secure profit.

Stop Loss (SL): Closes your position at a set price to prevent further losses.

How to Adjust Your Brackets

Once you have an active trade, managing your exits is a simple two-step process directly on the chart:

Step 1: Drag & Drop Locate the TP (Take Profit) or SL (Stop Loss) labels on your chart. Simply click and drag the label to your desired new price level.

Step 2: Confirm After moving the label, the Exits panel will appear (as seen in the screenshot). Review your new price or tick distance and click the red Confirm button to finalize the change.
​

Your orders are not updated until you click Confirm. Always ensure the side panel reflects your intended price before finalizing.

 

Buy and Sell Actions

BUY submits long orders

SELL submits short orders

Orders are sent instantly after confirmation based on your current configuration.
​

 

Flatten All

 

 

Immediately exits all positions and cancels all working orders.

This is your emergency exit button.

Best Practices

To ensure a smooth trading experience and avoid execution errors, follow these simple guidelines:

Confirm Quantity & Type: Always double-check your order size and whether you are using a Market or Limit order before hitting the button.

Use Brackets: Always attach a Stop Loss and Take Profit to every trade to automate your risk management.

Flatten with Caution: Avoid hovering over the Flatten button unless you intend to exit all positions immediately; this action is instant and final.

Market, Limit, and Stop Orders
Market, Limit, and Stop Orders

ArcTrader allows traders to choose between different order types depending on how they want to enter or manage a trade.

October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

 

The most common order types are:

Market

Limit

Stop

Market Orders

 

A Market order is used to buy or sell immediately at the best available market price.

Market orders are commonly used when:

You want immediate execution

Speed is more important than exact price

The market is liquid

You are entering quickly

You are exiting quickly

Important notes:

Market orders do not guarantee a specific fill price.

The final fill price may differ from the displayed price.

Slippage can occur during fast market movement.

Market orders should be used carefully during volatile periods.

Limit Orders

 

A Limit order is used to buy or sell at a specific price or better.

Limit orders are commonly used when:

You want a specific entry price

You do not want to chase the market

You are waiting for price to pull back

You want more control over execution price

Important notes:

Limit orders do not guarantee execution.

Price must reach your limit level.

The order may remain working if the market does not trade at that level.

The market can move away without filling your order.

Stop Orders

 

A Stop order becomes active once price reaches the stop level.

Stop orders are commonly used when:

Entering after a breakout

Exiting a losing trade

Protecting a position

Managing risk

Important notes:

Stop orders may trigger during fast market movement.

Once triggered, execution may occur at a different price.

Stop orders do not always guarantee the exact stop price.

Slippage may occur.

Best Practices

When choosing an order type:

Use Market orders carefully during volatility.

Use Limit orders when price control matters.

Use Stop orders when managing risk or breakout entries.

Always confirm order direction.

Review order levels before submitting.

Confirm whether the order is Buy or Sell.

Summary

Market, Limit, and Stop orders give traders different ways to enter and manage trades.

Choosing the correct order type is important for:

Execution

Risk management

Trade planning

Take Profit and Stop Loss
October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM
What is Take Profit?

 

Take Profit is an exit order designed to close a trade at a selected profit target.

Traders may use Take Profit to:

Lock in gains

Set a planned exit level

Reduce emotional decision-making

Automate part of trade management

Close a trade when price reaches a target

What is Stop Loss?

 

 

Stop Loss is an exit order designed to close a trade if price moves against the position.

Traders may use Stop Loss to:

Limit downside risk

Follow a trading plan

Avoid holding losing trades too long

Protect account drawdown

Manage risk more consistently

How Can Exits Be Set?

Depending on platform availability, exits may be configured by:

Price

Ticks

Risk amount

Other supported settings

Important Notes

Please keep the following in mind:

Take Profit and Stop Loss settings should be reviewed before submitting.

Exit orders may be affected by fast market conditions.

Stop Loss orders do not guarantee an exact fill price.

Exit levels may need to meet platform or symbol requirements.

Traders are responsible for confirming their risk before placing trades.

Best Practices

Before using exits:

Confirm your entry order first.

Choose a realistic profit target.

Use a stop level that matches your risk plan.

Avoid placing stops too close to normal market noise.

Confirm whether exits are attached correctly.

Review active orders after placing the trade.

 


​

For updated instructions on how to connect ATAS to Rithmic, please visit their connection guide.

 

There are two ways to connect your Rithmic account to ATAS: 

Directly

Via RTrader Pro.

Below, you'll find instructions for both methods.

Connecting Your Rithmic Account Directly to ATAS

To connect your Rithmic account directly, follow these steps:

Configure the Connection

In the ATAS platform’s main window, click on Connections > Add > Rithmic, then click Next.
​

Sign the Agreement

You will see windows for signing an agreement. Follow the on-screen instructions.

 

OCO Orders Warning

Keep in mind that OCO (One Cancels Other) orders are simulated locally on your computer. If you get disconnected and one of the OCO orders executes, the others WILL NOT be canceled. If you're okay with this, click I Accept, Please Continue.

 

Enter Your Credentials

Make sure your Rithmic account is NOT connected to RTrader Pro or any other platform.

Enter your Rithmic account login and password.

 

Select Your Server

Choose the appropriate server based on your account type and broker.

 

Optional: Aggregated Quotes

If you want, activate the checkbox for Aggregated Quotes to simplify market data. This reduces CPU load but might also slow data updates.

 

Uncheck "Connect via RTrader Pro"

Ensure the box next to Connect via RTrader Pro is unchecked.

 

You may be required to pay a subscription fee to connect to Rithmic servers:

 

Connecting Your Rithmic Account to ATAS via RTrader Pro

To connect your Rithmic account through RTrader Pro:

One Account Limitation

You can only connect one Rithmic account to ATAS via RTrader Pro.

Matching Settings

The settings for ATAS and RTrader Pro must match.

Log In to RTrader Pro

Log in to RTrader Pro, ensuring the following settings are activated:

Allow Plugins: [ON]

Aggregated Quotes: [ON]

Configure the Rithmic Connector in ATAS

In ATAS, go to the Rithmic connector settings and check the boxes next to:

Aggregated Quotes

Connect via RTrader Pro

Optional: Aggregated Quotes

You can enable Aggregated Quotes if you wish to simplify the market data and reduce CPU load.

Finalizing Your Connection

After configuring your connection, it will show up as a separate line in the connection list. Here’s what each column represents:

Add: Add a new connection.

Type: The connection source.

Name: You can name the connection however you like.

Status: Displays the connection status.

Quote Provider: Choose this connection as a quote provider if necessary.

Auto-Connect: Enable this if you want the connection to automatically occur when the platform starts.

Connection Settings Button: Click this to adjust settings.

Remove Connection: Use this to remove a connection from the list.

Connect/Disconnect: To manually connect or disconnect.
​

Important Notes About Rithmic Connections

Rithmic connections can be sensitive to communication issues and CPU load, so be aware of the following potential issues:

Plug-In Issues

If you enable the plugin connection, you won’t be able to connect without the plugin until you restart the application.

Multiple Connections

If you create two connections (one with the plugin and one without), the second one won’t connect.

Server Availability

If a Rithmic server is unavailable, the connection may take a long time to close, causing delays. Switching servers may require waiting for the previous connection to fully close.

Connection Lost

If the connection is lost, ATAS will notify you with a pop-up message.

Potential Connection Loss

If there’s an issue with data exchange between Rithmic and ATAS, you’ll receive messages like:
“PnL Connection - Heartbeat has been quiet for XX seconds.”

These messages might indicate problems with the PnL, trading, or historical data connections.

Actions to Take in Case of Connection Issues

PnL Connection Issues:

Data like price, volume, and position direction on ATAS may differ from Rithmic’s servers.

Trading Connection Issues:

Orders may be sent to Rithmic, but their status might not be reflected in ATAS.

Handling Alerts:

If you receive messages like "PnL Connection - Heartbeat has been quiet for XX seconds", ATAS will show a pop-up with the details.

Order Confirmation After Alerts:

When you receive such messages, ATAS will require confirmation for any new orders or changes to your position. This confirmation will display all previous Rithmic messages you’ve received.
​

 

DayTraders only offers limited support for platform related issues. If you experience any issues with your platform, please contact their platform support directly.

Accessing Onyx from Your Phone
October 22, 2026
Copy for LLM

Onyx Released mobile apps for both iOS and Android that you can find in the links below:

 

iOS: https://apps.apple.com/co/app/onyx-mobile-trader/id6749869310?l=en-GB

 

Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tradeshell.onyxmobiletrader&hl=en-US

 

To log in, you will use your Rithmic credentials.

 

How to Access Onyx on your Browser

Open Safari or Chrome on your phone.

Go to:
​https://daytraders.onyx-trader.com

Log in using your Rithmic username and password.

The interface automatically adjusts to your screen size.

 

What You Can Do on Mobile

 

 

Onyx gives you access to core trading features on mobile:

 

Trading and Order Management

Place Market, Limit, and Stop orders

Use Simple or Bracket orders

Flatten positions instantly

Monitor open orders and positions

Account Monitoring

View balance and PnL

Check account status

Track open trades

Review trading limits

Charts

Access TradingView charts

Switch symbols and timeframes

Apply and view indicators

Zoom and navigate charts

Journal and History

View your Trading Journal

Browse the calendar

Review performance by day

Access trade history

 

Important Mobile Trading Warning

Trading from a phone should be done with caution.

 

Mobile networks can be unstable and may disconnect without warning.

 

We strongly recommend:

Never leave active trades unattended

Avoid trading in poor signal areas

Do not rely on mobile for prolonged trading sessions

Use mobile mainly for monitoring and emergency trade management

Keep rTrader Pro open to manage your positions

If your connection drops unexpectedly, you may lose the ability to manage your position in real time.

 

Best Practices

For better stability:

Use WiFi with a strong signal

Keep the browser session active

Avoid switching apps while trading

Use desktop for primary execution

Limitations on Mobile

Desktop is recommended for:

Performance monitoring

Multi-chart layouts

Execution-intensive trading

Connectivity diagnostics

Mobile access is best suited for management, not full-time execution.

 

Troubleshooting

If charts freeze or orders delay:

Refresh the browser

Restart your network

Switch to WiFi or a stronger signal

Contact support if problems continue
​

Mobile Backgrounding & Connection Behavior

When using Onyx on a mobile phone, the operating system (iOS or Android) may pause or suspend the browser page when:

The phone is locked

The browser is sent to the background

You switch apps or tabs

Battery or power-saving features activate

When this happens, the live connection used for charts, positions, and order updates may be interrupted. As a result, the platform can appear frozen or unresponsive until a full reconnect occurs.

This is a limitation of mobile browsers and OS power-management behavior, not a platform failure.

 

What to Do If This Happens

Refresh the browser page

Or fully close the tab and reopen it

Log back in if prompted and confirm data reloads

How to Reduce Occurrences

Keep the Onyx tab in the foreground while trading

Avoid locking your phone during active trades

Disable Low Power Mode while trading (if enabled)

Use mobile primarily for monitoring and trade management

While Onyx includes auto-reconnect logic, mobile browsers can still interrupt background connections intermittently. For this reason, desktop trading remains the recommended setup for active execution.

Optimizing Onyx Performance (VPS)

 

Onyx now includes a built-in Connection Quality Monitor that helps you understand your internet performance and how it may impact your trading.

 

This feature runs automatically in the background and gives you real-time visibility into your connection quality.

Where to Find It

 

You’ll see a new connection indicator in the top header of the platform, next to your account status.

Displays your download speed

Color-coded for quick visibility

Click the indicator to view full connection details.

Connection Quality Indicator

The indicator is color-coded based on your connection speed:

Green: 50+ Mbps (Optimal)

Yellow: 25–50 Mbps (Moderate)

Red: Below 25 Mbps (Poor)

For the best trading experience, Onyx recommends a stable connection of 50 Mbps or higher.

View Detailed Connection Metrics

When you click the indicator, you’ll see:

Download speed

Upload speed

Ping (latency)

Jitter

These metrics help you understand your connection stability and identify potential issues affecting execution or chart performance.

How It Works

The connection test runs automatically once per day when you load the platform

It runs silently in the background

It does not impact your trading performance

It provides a quick snapshot for both you and support teams

This allows faster troubleshooting if you experience lag, delays, or disconnects.
